subject: Access logs: retention window, export formats, and deletion attestations
messages:
From: security@halcyonpharma.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: access/audit log retention and export — Halcyon PHI scope

Hi Maya,

We're preparing for a compliance review focused on PHI-handling workloads. Two quick asks so we can close our evidence bundle:  

1) For tenant-scoped access and audit logs (console/API/management plane), what is the default retention window in Redwood Hosted for our EU and US tenants and what export formats do you support for bulk delivery?  
2) When Halcyon requests a one-off bulk export (scheduled snapshot), can Redwood provide a signed deletion attestation after we confirm successful transfer? If so, what granularity does the attestation cover (per-export, per-tenant, per-object)?

Goal: we need clear language for our SOC file and an indicative timeline (how long exports take and how long you keep the exported copy before purge).

Thanks — we can hop on a short call if that's easier.

— Priya Rao
Security Lead, Halcyon Pharma
security@halcyonpharma.com
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
To: security@halcyonpharma.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit log retention and export — Halcyon PHI scope

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the clear ask — happy to help and can provide the formal language you can drop into the SOC bundle. Summary up front:  

- Default retention (hosted): 90 days for access/audit trails on standard Hosted tenants; can be extended to 365 days with a retention add-on or via Dedicated/Private deployments. EU and US tenants follow the same retention defaults unless you have a region-specific retention contract.
- Export formats: bulk exports are provided as compressed JSON lines (ndjson.gz) for audit entries, with an accompanying CSV manifest that includes object keys, time ranges, and checksum. We also support a gzipped CSV export on request (larger size). Exports are delivered to customer-owned S3 (pre-signed PUT) or to our signed SFTP endpoint per your preference.
- One-off export purge & attestation: yes — we can issue a signed deletion attestation. Attestations are issued per-export (export ID) and include timestamp, export checksum, recipient endpoint, and a declaration that Redwood deleted its temporary/export staging copy. For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide a more granular chain-of-custody statement on request.

Operational timelines (indicative):
- Snapshot preparation: typically 1–6 hours for 30–90 days of logs (depends on time range and tenant size).
- Transfer time: depends on network and delivery method; S3 pre-signed PUTs are fastest.
- Attestation delivery: within 48 hours of your confirmation that the transfer was successful.

I'll attach our export playbook and an example manifest. Kim and Marcus — please confirm that the attestation template we've been using still matches the legal template for 3rd-party evidence (I copied the relevant section into the playbook).

If that fits your needs I can start a formal export request and share the S3 details.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Customer Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood_audit_playbook_v2.pdf, sample_manifest.csv
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit log retention and export — Halcyon PHI scope

Maya — quick confirmations:  

- Attestation: template v2 looks good to me; confirms per-export signed deletion statement. Legal suggested a small addition to include the internal job-id used for the purge (helps tie to internal audit trails).
- Retention messaging: call out that retention extension requires a signed amendment for Hosted (we should add that sentence to the playbook).

Marcus — any infra constraints on delivery SLA for very large snapshots (1TB+ of ndjson.gz)? We should set expectation if prep > 6 hours.

Thanks — K

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Customer Security Operations
kimberly@redwood.com
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit log retention and export — Halcyon PHI scope

Ack. For very large exports (multiple TB) prep can run into longer job queueing and packaging time; realistic window is 6–24 hours depending on the bucket window and whether compression can be parallelized across shards. If they need guaranteed <6h, recommend a Dedicated export SLA or staged exports (by date ranges). Also confirming we include internal purge job-id in attestation payload (we can redact internal hostnames).

I'll flag any potential quota throttles if the job is scheduled the same day as heavy snapshot runs.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Engineering Lead, Data Export Platform
marcus@redwood.com
From: security@halcyonpharma.com
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit log retention and export — Halcyon PHI scope

Thanks — helpful. Two follow-ups before we kick off the request:  

1) Can you provide the exact wording Redwood will accept in our SOC folder for the attestation line? We want copy-paste language to avoid legal back-and-forth.
2) For exports delivered to our S3, will Redwood keep any cached/staging copies in your environment beyond the point of transfer (i.e., short-lived staging for transfer)? If so, please confirm the maximum TTL for those staging copies prior to automatic purge.

If you can send the attestation wording and confirm TTL we can schedule the export next week.

— Priya
Priya Rao
Security Lead, Halcyon Pharma
security@halcyonpharma.com
